final_proof:
Let $L$ be a locale, and write $\mathcal O(L)$ for its frame of opens. Recall that a locale morphism $g:A\to B$ is represented contravariantly by its inverse-image frame homomorphism $g^*:\mathcal O(B)\to\mathcal O(A)$, and that $(h\circ g)^*=g^*\circ h^*$. A point of $L$ is a locale morphism $p:1\to L$, equivalently a frame homomorphism $p^*:\mathcal O(L)\to\mathbf 2$. For $a\in\mathcal O(L)$, put
\[
U_a=\{p\in\operatorname{Sp}(L):p^*(a)=1\}.
\]
These sets are the opens defining the topology on $\operatorname{Sp}(L)$ (indeed, $U_{\bigvee_i a_i}=\bigcup_iU_{a_i}$ and $U_{a\wedge a'}=U_a\cap U_{a'}$). By the definition of the counit of the spectrum adjunction, its component
\[
\sigma_L:\mathbf\Omega\operatorname{Sp}(L)\longrightarrow L
\]
has inverse-image frame homomorphism
\[
\sigma_L^*:\mathcal O(L)\longrightarrow\mathcal O(\operatorname{Sp}(L)),\qquad a\longmapsto U_a.
\]

We verify naturality. Let $f:L\to M$ be an arbitrary locale morphism. The induced continuous map on spectra is
\[
\operatorname{Sp}(f):\operatorname{Sp}(L)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Sp}(M),\qquad p\longmapsto f\circ p.
\]
For every $b\in\mathcal O(M)$ and every point $p$ of $L$, the composition rule for inverse images gives
\[
(f\circ p)^*(b)=p^*(f^*(b)).
\]
Consequently,
\[
\operatorname{Sp}(f)^{-1}(U_b)
=\{p:(f\circ p)^*(b)=1\}
=\{p:p^*(f^*(b))=1\}
=U_{f^*(b)}.
\tag{1}
\]
(In particular, this calculation also shows directly that $\operatorname{Sp}(f)$ is continuous.)

The naturality square to be proved is
\[
f\circ\sigma_L=\sigma_M\circ\mathbf\Omega\operatorname{Sp}(f),
\]
whose two sides are locale morphisms $\mathbf\Omega\operatorname{Sp}(L)\to M$. Locale morphisms are equal if their inverse-image frame homomorphisms are equal. For an arbitrary $b\in\mathcal O(M)$, the inverse image along the left-hand side is
\[
(f\circ\sigma_L)^*(b)=\sigma_L^*(f^*(b))=U_{f^*(b)}.
\]
On the other hand, the inverse-image homomorphism of the locale morphism $\mathbf\Omega\operatorname{Sp}(f)$ is ordinary inverse image along the continuous map $\operatorname{Sp}(f)$. Hence, using (1),
\[
(\sigma_M\circ\mathbf\Omega\operatorname{Sp}(f))^*(b)
=(\mathbf\Omega\operatorname{Sp}(f))^*(\sigma_M^*(b))
=\operatorname{Sp}(f)^{-1}(U_b)
=U_{f^*(b)}.
\]
Thus the two composites have the same inverse-image homomorphism and are equal. Since $f:L\to M$ was arbitrary, all naturality squares commute. Therefore $\sigma:\mathbf\Omega\operatorname{Sp}\Rightarrow\operatorname{id}_{\mathbf{Loc}}$ is a natural transformation.
